sentences.text: Hauffiopteryx was a relatively small ichthyosaur that reached lengths between 2 and 3 meters, though the lectotype specimen measures approximately 1.93 meters in length.
This animal possessed a short, very thin snout that tapered to a sharp point.
The tooth crowns of Hauffiopteryx had smooth outer surfaces, with the rear teeth being larger than the front ones.
The eye sockets of Hauffiopteryx typicus were notably large and circular.
The dorsal ribs of Hauffiopteryx were strongly forked at their upper ends, giving them a double-headed appearance.
Unlike the four main digits in the forelimbs, each hindlimb of Hauffiopteryx possessed only three main digits.
The type specimen is an articulated complete skeleton that preserved the skull and some soft tissues.
In Hauffiopteryx, the fibula is significantly larger than the tibia.
The parent group of Hauffiopteryx is Neoichthyosauria.
Hauffiopteryx is classified in the class Reptilia.

Hauffiopteryx fossils from Germany and Luxembourg date to the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, between approximately 182.7 and 181.8 million years ago, while the overall time range for the genus is the Toarcian, from 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.
The time range for Hauffiopteryx is the Toarcian, from 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.

In Hauffiopteryx altera, the highest points of the upper jaw are located behind the nostrils, whereas in H. typicus they are located beneath them. The lacrimal bones differ between species: they are triradiate in H. typicus but massive and triangular in H. altera.
